direction: W: Watchmaker hands. The hands themselves become the logo, as four distinct real watch-hand styles, each with a deliberate collet (hub) and exact 5:00 geometry.
notes:
Build: everything is generated by /home/user/offshft/designs/mark/explore/W/build.cjs, which uses a small geometry library at /home/user/offshft/designs/mark/explore/W/lib.cjs. Rerun with `node build.cjs` (set CHECK_LOCKUP=1 to also run the slow true-size lockup checks). Each outline is a single clean path with true arcs for collets and leaves; there are no overlapping pieces except W4's two-tone layers.

5:00 check: the hands are built on kit.polar and kit.FIVE. Measured tip angles are exactly 0.000 and 150.000 degrees in all four. Hour reach is about 0.63 of minute reach (5:8).

Embroidery check: each mark is rendered with its longest side at 25 mm (40 px/mm). Thread thinner than 1.2 mm and gaps narrower than 1.2 mm are found by morphological open/close with a 1.2 mm disk, separately for each thread colour. Only points and inside corners are flagged. Lockups were also checked at true size (cap 7 mm): mark and wordmark pass, apart from corner rounding on letters and W4's points. Diagnostic images are in /home/user/offshft/designs/mark/explore/W/check.

What I learned and fixed:
1. On the 150 degree hour hand, a 60 degree point puts one tip edge exactly vertical and it looks chopped off. W1 and W3 use 90 degree square points, W4 uses 40 degree points, and the leaves are curved.
2. A counterweight tail at 6 o'clock sits only 30 degrees from the 5 o'clock hour hand. The wedge between them stays under 1.2 mm for about 5 mm out from the pivot and fills in, which recreates the blob. It is rejected for geometric reasons.
3. A symmetric leaf on the 5 o'clock diagonal reads as drooping. W2 has an 8% optical correction.
4. Breguet moon hands were explored and rejected: busy (three rings), chain-like, and they fill in at 13 mm. Sketches are in /home/user/offshft/designs/mark/explore/W/sketch.

Lockup system:
- The collet centre sits on the baseline. At the chosen scale the mark's box is also centred on the cap height, so both rules hold at once (mark is about 3.4 times the cap height).
- The gap from the collet to the O is 0.8 times the word space between OFF and SHFT.
- Cap height is 7 mm. Lockups are 88 to 93 mm wide, which fits the 4 in front panel, and the mark sits at 0.95 scale so the 1.2 mm minimum still holds.
- Wordmarks: W1 xbold tracked 0.16 em, W3 xbold 0.14 em, W4 xbold 0.18 em, W2 xsemi 0.22 em for a lighter, airier pairing.

Extras in each variant folder: mark-small.svg and sizes-small.png (13 mm versions: no holes or channels, slightly heavier hands) and lockup-dark.svg/.png on Spruce. No version uses more than 2 thread colours.

Recommendation: W1 is the strongest all-rounder. Choose W3 for more presence and a two-colour story, or W4 two-tone as the premium option. W2 is the weakest.

Before adopting any of these, run a trademark clearance search, as AGENTS.md requires. Clock-hand marks are a crowded space.

variants.name: Pin
variants.concept: Parallel baton hands with square 90-degree points on a collet with a punched pin hole. Everything is sized on a 0.6 mm grid: minute 4 units wide, hour 6, collet 9, pin 3, reaches 27 and 17. The pin hole turns two strokes into a mechanism, so it no longer reads as a bent stick.
variants.weaknesses: The silhouette is tall and narrow (about 1:3), which is inherent to 5:00, so it has modest presence from a distance. The shapes are fairly expected; the pin hole is the one truly ownable detail, and it fills in below about 20 mm, so the 13 mm version (mark-small.svg) is solid.

variants.name: Leaf
variants.concept: Feuille (leaf) hands drawn as pure circular-arc lenses on a pinned collet. The hour leaf carries an 8% optical correction so it does not droop on the diagonal. It has dress-watch elegance and a quiet nod to time spent outdoors.
variants.weaknesses: Even with the correction, the hour leaf on the 5 o'clock diagonal still reads a little like a propeller blade or claw, so the clock read depends on the pinned collet. The leaf points are sharp, so about the last 1.5 mm stitches as a taper, and the 13 mm version reads close to a sprout.

variants.name: Lume
variants.concept: Tool-watch hands drawn with one 1.3 mm wall: outlined batons with rounded lume channels and a ring hub. In two colours the channels fill with Sun thread, the glow after dark. It has the most presence of the four.
variants.weaknesses: It is the heaviest and busiest of the four. The 1.3 mm walls only just clear the rule (1.24 mm inside the lockup). At 13 mm the channels and ring cannot hold 1.2 mm, so the side-of-hat version falls back to solid batons and loses the lume idea.

variants.name: Dauphine
variants.concept: Faceted dauphine blades with 40-degree points on a large polished collet, lit from the left. The two-tone versions (Rust/Ink on light fabric, Bone/Sun on dark) make the facets read as real light; in one colour it is the plain silhouette. It is the most crafted, premium-feeling option.
variants.weaknesses: The one-colour silhouette (mark.svg) is clearly weaker than the two-tone and reads a bit like a spire or spear. Inside the 40-degree points each facet colour narrows below 1.2 mm for about the last 3.5 mm, so the digitizer has to finish the points as a two-colour taper or in one colour.
